params.body:
The photo editor that replaced Toast UI (#950) lost the handle that turned a cover. A plate photographed at an angle could only be covered by a level rectangle, which either leaves the plate's ends readable or covers much more of the car than needed. This came up on 5 October 2026 while blurring a plate on a car of Garage Palermo.

## What changes

- A selected cover shows a knob on a short stick above its top edge. Dragging the knob turns the cover around its centre. Within 3 degrees of level (or of a quarter turn) it snaps straight, and a straight cover stores no angle at all, so existing state and undo snapshots are unchanged.
- A turned cover is hit on its turned shape, moves as before, and resizes along its own sides with the opposite corner fixed.
- Fill and outline are drawn in a frame turned around the centre. Blur works out the upright box around the turned cover, keeps the blur strength of the cover's own sides, and clips to the turned shape.
- Save goes through the same `drawScene`, so the saved photo holds the turned cover.
- Only covers turn. Circles and pen lines are unchanged.
- R S1-6.45 now describes the knob.

## Tests

`npm run test:js`: 103 passed, including new tests for the snap, the bounding box, turning by the knob (plus undo and snapping back), hitting and resizing a turned cover, a turned black cover read back pixel by pixel, and a turned blur that blurs the slant and leaves the corners of its upright box sharp. `eslint` is clean, `npm run build` passes, and `bin/rules-sources` reports no problems.

Not yet tried by hand on a phone or with a mouse in a browser.
params.title: A cover in the photo editor turns to fit a slanted plate
